logs.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the fastest-growing ever, with cases surging above 1,000 and the death toll reaching 600. The outbreak has spread to new provinces including Tshopo and Haut-Uele, and the first case outside Africa has been confirmed in France. Response efforts are hampered by funding shortages, unpaid health workers, and the closure of USAID, while new diagnostic tests and treatment trials offer hope.

As a key part of its annual 'MSF Day' campaign, the exhibition will tour three locations throughout July: The Wai, Festival Walk, and TKO Plaza. It showcases real-life stories of MSF providing emergency medical humanitarian assistance to people affected by protracted conflicts and crises. The event also features an Ebola disease-themed zone, which aims to deepen public awareness and understanding of the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

logs.summary:
As of August 12, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has topped 4,000 cases, and the CDC is implementing measures to prevent the virus from entering the United States. The death toll has surpassed 2,000, and the World Health Organization warns the outbreak is on track to become the deadliest in history.
The outbreak has spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, with a death recorded after an infected person traveled from Isiro. The DRC has submitted an emergency request for Ervebo from the global stockpile for use against the Bundibugyo strain, reversing the WHO's May guidance. The WHO warns the outbreak is on track to surpass the deadliest in history (which killed over 11,000), as CDC measures to prevent entry into the US continue.

The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, after an infected person traveled from Isiro, resulting in a confirmed death there. The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has spread to a sixth province, Bas-Uele, after a death was recorded there, as confirmed by Africa CDC. Oxfam warns of a lack of resources for response teams. logs.summary:
On August 5, 2026, a magnitude 6.4–7.0 earthquake struck off the coast of Sarangani, Davao Occidental, at 12:13 PM local time, jolting parts of Mindanao. PHIVOLCS confirmed the tremor was an aftershock of the destructive June 26 magnitude 7.8 earthquake and reported no tsunami threat. While no damage or casualties were immediately reported, several provinces suspended classes and work as a precaution, and the quake caused panic among residents.
On August 6, 2026, a magnitude 6.3 aftershock struck off Balut Island in Sarangani, Davao Occidental, along with magnitude 5.6 and 5.3 quakes, all part of the ongoing seismic sequence following the June 26 magnitude 7.8 earthquake. In related aftermath reports, police stations in areas affected by the August 5 magnitude 6.4 quake remained operational, and a crowd at a Mindanao subsidy site was rattled but no casualties were reported.

logs.summary: Throughout late July 2026, the wildfire incident in southern France's Pyrénées-Orientales area escalated dramatically amid a broader crisis of wildfires across southwestern France and Spain. Massive fires forced over 360,000 people to evacuate, with the blaze near Bordeaux prompting 84,000 to return home on July 30 as cooler weather arrived, while a separate fast-moving fire in the Var department flared on July 22. Romania extended its firefighting mission by two weeks, and French firefighters created tree-cutting firebreaks as they described the system at breaking point, with President Macron calling the situation France's biggest challenge since WWII.

logs.summary:
Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

news.headline: Ukraine HITS Russian Train carrying North Korean KN-23 and KN-24 Ballistic Missiles in Shock Attack - Oneindia
news.body: A massive blast has reportedly struck a strategic railway deep inside Russia, with Ukraine claiming the target was a train allegedly carrying North Korean KN-23 and KN-24 ballistic missiles and ammunition. The reported operation took place along the Trans-Siberian Railway, thousands of kilometres from the Ukrainian front. Ukrainian military expert Kyrylo Sazonov, citing sources linked to Ukraine’s HUR intelligence agency, said operatives had tracked the strategic cargo from the North Korean border. The alleged sabotage reportedly involved remotely controlled explosives placed beneath the tracks. When the train passed over the suspected blast site, the explosives were allegedly detonated, disrupting a crucial weapons supply route.- Watch Video on English Oneindia

logs.summary:
The U.S. and Iran have paused attacks and resumed diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, with mediators reporting progress and talks focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, the Pentagon quietly removed four recent troop deaths from its official Iran war death toll, reclassifying them in a new category, sparking controversy. Additional concerns include the U.S.'s dangerously low weaponry supply and growing public skepticism over the war’s costs and duration.
Mediators reported that neither the U.S. nor Iran conducted any attacks for three consecutive days, signaling progress in ceasefire efforts. New polls indicate that only one in three Americans now support the war, the lowest reading since the conflict began, and a majority view it as going "very badly." The Pentagon continued to face scrutiny over its reclassification of four troop deaths from the conflict.

logs.summary:
The U.S. announced plans for unprecedented economic sanctions and a continued naval blockade against Iran, with Treasury Secretary Bessent warning of a "one-two punch." Two UAE-operated ADNOC oil tankers were struck by Iranian drones in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting fresh accusations from the UAE. President Trump defended the USS Lincoln's record-length deployment as "not nearly long enough," while Israel expressed shock at the pace of Iran's military recovery and an oil spill from a struck vessel reached Iran's Qeshm Island, causing environmental damage.
President Trump threatened to declare the Strait of Hormuz a U.S. territory, prompting Iran to forcefully reject the claim and insist the waterway "will remain Iranian." Iran's IRGC commander boasted that the war effort proves Islam can "rule the world," while the U.S. widened its diplomatic outreach to Austria and Greece amid stalled talks. Trump also warned Americans to brace for continued high fuel prices, and the U.S. pulled its last aircraft carrier from Asia to focus on the conflict.

Progress towards peace talks remained stalled, with oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz also halted. Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the waterway would remain under Tehran’s control until Washington accepted what he described as the reality of defeat. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Iran had not decided to resume talks with the US, adding that messages exchanged through Qatar and Pakistan did not constitute negotiations. Separate discussions with Oman were focused on establishing a sea route through the Strait, he said. Meanwhile, Qatar on Saturday denied claims that it was holding Iranian pilots, saying they had violated Qatari airspace in March and failed to respond to repeated attempts to contact them.

logs.summary:
A powerful earthquake, initially measured at magnitude 7.1 (later revised to 6.8), struck Kumamoto Prefecture in southern Japan on July 28, 2026, at 4:27 p.m. local time. The quake caused the partial collapse of the Aeon Mall in Kashima, trapping many people and leaving an unknown number dead, while injuring at least 50 others and causing widespread damage including fires, power outages, and damage to historic Kumamoto Castle.
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck southern Japan's Kyushu island near Kumamoto on July 28, 2026, causing a shopping mall to partially collapse with multiple people trapped and feared dead. The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes, ruptured roads, triggered a temporary tsunami advisory, and left dozens injured, with up to 30 mall employees missing after an explosion.

news.headline: Prime minister visits quake-hit southern Japan as cleanup begins in intense heat
news.body: Residents of Japan’s quake-hit southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto are working to clear their homes in intense heat, as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi briefly visited Kumamoto Prefecture on Monday for the first time since a magnitude 7.1 quake last Tuesday. The heat and a lack of water have added to the challenges in the severely damaged areas. The quake killed 38 people, including one who died of apparent heat stroke while taking shelter in a car in hot weather. Residents put out heaps of debris, broken furniture and damaged appliances for collection, while in the towns of Uki and Hikawa, construction of temporary housing began.

incidents.summary:
New drought developments include Hungary sinking two barges near its nuclear plant to ensure cooling as the Danube remains at record lows, and drought conditions expanding across Missouri amid extreme summer heat. In Europe, ancient 'hunger stones' are re-emerging in receding rivers, and low water in Rome’s Tiber has exposed the ruins of Nero’s Bridge. Federal forecasters warn of a potentially historically strong El Niño event, while the UK announced a £65m funding boost for drought-hit farmers and a runner is undertaking a long-distance trek along the Colorado River to document the drought's impact.
New drought impacts include a spike in roadkill in Wyoming as wildlife seeks food and water near roadsides, and an escalating fodder crisis in Ireland prompting a government meeting with farm organizations. In the Netherlands, exposed riverbeds due to low water have become a boon for archaeologists searching for buried treasures. Separately, relentless heat and drought could halve France's maize crop, adding to EU harvest losses.

logs.summary:
A severe drought is affecting multiple regions globally as of late July 2026. In Europe, an "exceptionally serious" drought has hit half of England and all of Wales, while the Rhine River dropped to its lowest ever level in the Netherlands and the Danube reached record lows in Budapest, disrupting tourism and industry. news.headline: Record-low Danube River affects tourism and industry as drought and heat grip Central Europe
news.body: As wildfires and successive heatwaves in France and Spain highlight climate change's impact, a severe drought is causing record low water levels on the Danube River, affecting tourism and industry. The river, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows, exposing rocks and old shipwrecks. In Budapest, the Danube was measured at just 23 centimeters, breaking previous records. River cruise ships are docking upriver, and sightseeing cruises have been canceled. The drought has also affected Hungary and Romania's nuclear power plant operations, exposed a World War II bomb, and ended the summer season for excursion boat operators in Serbia.

logs.summary:
The global drought continues to worsen with new impacts: in Africa, Somalia sees thousands fleeing a yearslong drought as hunger deepens and aid shrinks, with about 2 million people facing emergency food insecurity. Europe's drought intensifies as the UK experiences its hottest summer on record, prompting drought declarations, an amber heat alert, warnings on rail travel, and calls to remove disposable BBQs after over 1,000 wildfires, while Italy's Po River runs low in Turin. In the US, Colorado reports a 219% jump in bear sightings due to historic drought, Virginia designates 125 localities as drought disaster areas, and the World Meteorological Organization notes July 2026 was the second warmest July on record, while a massive El Niño is already causing dry spells and crop failures on three continents.
July 2026 was the second warmest July on record globally. Europe's drought intensifies: the Rhine River's low levels threaten Germany's economy, France faces drinking water shortages in some regions with water deliveries by truck, Britain records its hottest day of the year at 38°C and faces a fifth heat wave, and crops from Dutch potatoes to Bosnian corn are shriveling. In the US, Georgia's extreme drought is declared over after summer rains, while North Carolina sees some drought easing but exceptional drought persists in Brunswick County. Somalia's yearslong drought continues to drive thousands from rural communities into displacement as hunger deepens.

logs.summary:
Greece faced severe wildfires in late July and early August 2026, with a major blaze northwest of Athens destroying over 100 homes and burning thousands of hectares. On August 2, two firefighting helicopters collided in mid-air near Psatha, killing two crew members. By August 3, water-dropping aircraft continued to battle the fires, which had been fueled by extreme winds and record-breaking heat, with over 200 fires reported across the country since July 27.
On August 3, the wildfire west of Athens flared up again, requiring continued water-bombing aircraft operations. By August 4, firefighters seized a break in high winds to reinforce containment lines, while some residents returned to damaged homes, though forecasters warned that stronger gusts and rising temperatures were expected to return. The blaze, part of over 200 fires across Greece since late July, remained a threat amid a record-breaking heatwave and drought.

news.headline: Wildfires Rage in Greece as Heat Wave Grips Europe
news.body: In Greece, two firefighters were killed Sunday when two helicopters battling a massive wildfire collided west of Athens. Two other crew members in one of the helicopters were rescued. More than 100 homes were destroyed overnight this weekend in blazes that broke out around the coastal village of Porto Germeno. Hundreds of people have been evacuated. This is a local resident. Giorgos Mavroidis: “It’s not a good situation. This is extremely sad. The wind is very strong and keeps changing direction. It’s difficult to deal with. The firefighters, who are trained and experienced, can’t contain it. How can we?” Meanwhile, Hungary has temporarily shut down the country’s sole nuclear power plant for the first time in more than four decades amid a scorching heat wave and severe drought that triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. In more related news, Britain’s National Farmers’ Union warns rising heat and a water drought could lead to shortages of certain foods in parts of England. This is at least the third drought in five years, with some areas of England not seeing rain in over a month. Here in the United States, in Washington state, nearly 65,000 people have received evacuation orders amid intensifying wildfires around the city of Spokane. Local officials say blazes in the region have destroyed more than 700 homes and businesses.

news.headline: Europe’s wildfire crisis eases in west as danger shifts east to Greece
news.body: Firefighters have contained a vast wildfire in southwestern France, allowing nearly 200,000 people to return home. The development comes after what may have been the country’s largest peacetime evacuation. However, renewed fires have forced thousands from their homes in other parts of France and Greece. In the Var region, a fire thought to be under control raced across 10 square kilometers in just six hours. Meanwhile, in Greece, gale-force winds have driven flames through the coastal area between Athens and Thebes, leading to evacuations. Rising temperatures and prolonged droughts are making Europe more vulnerable to such wildfires.

news.headline: As France tames wildfire and lets 84,000 evacuees go home, blazes flare across Europe
news.body: France has allowed 84,000 evacuees to return home after a massive wildfire, signaling progress in battling the flames. The fire has burned an area four times the size of Paris. However, wildfires continue to flare across Europe, fueled by an exceptionally hot and dry summer. Firefighters are tackling blazes in the U.K., Spain, Germany, Greece, and Turkey. Hollywood star George Clooney evacuated his French home due to a nearby fire. In France, authorities are using water cannons and international aid to control the situation. Cooler weather and rain are helping efforts, but conditions remain challenging.

A preliminary investigation suggests that a fault in a wind farm's power line may have sparked the devastating Attica-Boeotia wildfire. Rescue crews are working to reunite hundreds of animals displaced by the blaze, while Civil Protection warns of very high fire risk across multiple regions, including Attica, on August 5-6.
On August 6, the Aigosthena fortress near Porto Germeno was reported to have escaped major damage from the four-day wildfire, though some modern site infrastructure was affected.

Foreign firefighting and helicopter crews are often deployed in Greece to help tackle wildfires during the country’s hot, dry summers. The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe’s wildfire emergency.

Europe is the fastest-warming continent, with rising temperatures and droughts making wildfires more intense.

logs.summary:
On August 4, 2026, the Grasshopper Fire near Mt. Hood Meadows in Oregon has burned over 34,000 acres and is 19% contained, prompting Level 3 "go now" evacuation orders for the area. The fire has expanded westward toward the Mount Hood National Forest, with Clackamas County issuing Level 1 evacuations as well.
The Grasshopper Fire near Mt. Hood Meadows has burned 34,659 acres and remains 19% contained. Timberline Lodge was placed under a Level 1 evacuation notice, while Mt. Hood Meadows remains under Level 3 "Go Now" orders. Smoke from the fire is driving guests away from Timberline Lodge, which remains open.

logs.summary:
As of August 13, the death toll from the M7.4 earthquake in Colombia has risen to at least 273, with 377 people still missing, as rescue operations entered a "final phase" following the closure of the critical 72-hour survival window. Colombia declared a state of economic emergency to aid reconstruction, while international aid efforts expanded with community donation drives in Florida, New Jersey, and elsewhere, and benefit concerts were announced to support relief. The new far-right government under President Abelardo De La Espriella faced the ongoing crisis, with hopes of finding more survivors fading.
By August 13-14, the earthquake death toll rose to at least 281-285 with 379 people still missing, as rescue operations shifted to a grim recovery phase after the 72-hour survival window closed. International aid expanded with Zoomlion deploying heavy equipment and the EU pledging €2 million, while conspiracy theories falsely linked the quake to an Alaska research program and individual stories emerged of victims including a New Jersey mother and a California man. Colombia's new far-right government faced growing strain, with official death tolls reaching up to 285 and over 100,000 people affected, as the response drew comparisons to Venezuela's handling of recent twin quakes.

logs.summary:
As of August 14, the death toll from the M7.4 earthquake in Colombia rose to at least 285-287, with over 100,000 people affected and tens of thousands of homes damaged or destroyed. Rescue operations continued past the critical 72-hour survival window, with a dog rescued alive in Cali, while international aid expanded including a $200 million World Bank disbursement, Zoomlion heavy equipment deployment, and community fundraisers in the U.S. Geologists analyzed the quake's tectonic causes, and the new government faced growing strain in response efforts as search teams shifted toward a grim recovery phase.
Families angered by the slow pace of search operations in Cali voiced demands for answers, while Israeli Defense Forces rescue teams deployed to assist local authorities. The tragic discovery of the last triplet sister, Isabella Saavedra, in the rubble highlighted personal losses. Additionally, a cargo airline and Miami nonprofit organized an aid flight, and the ongoing response placed further strain on Colombia's new government.

logs.summary:
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia's Flores region near Ende on August 14, 2026, toppling buildings and killing at least two people. The shallow quake triggered a tsunami warning for four provinces, prompting mass evacuations before the alert was later lifted. Several strong aftershocks were reported.
The death toll from the magnitude 7.7 earthquake near Ende, Indonesia has risen to at least 38, with dozens injured and many buildings collapsed or damaged. Rescuers are searching for survivors in affected areas, and tsunami waves of less than 1 meter were recorded in several locations before the warning was lifted.

news.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia, tsunami warning issued - West Hawaii Today
news.body: JAKARTA (Reuters) — An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and several aftershocks struck off the coast of eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the nation’s geophysics agency BMKG said, while tsunami waves of less than 1 metre (3 feet) were recorded in several areas. Many rushed from their homes, but there were no initial reports of damage from the quake, which was felt strongly for around one minute in regions such as Nagekeo and Bima, said Dodi Yuleova, the spokesperson for the national disaster mitigation agency. A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as located at a port in Maumere, the main town in Sikka Regency on Flores Island in eastern Indonesia, showed parts of a building collapsing in dust and rubble as people screamed and ran in the street. A hospital in the district of Ende in East Nusa Tenggara Province was moving patients outside, Kompas TV footage showed. BMKG recorded the first quake at 4:58 a.m. (2158 GMT) at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), followed by several aftershocks.

logs.summary: The death toll from the August 14 M7.7 earthquake off Flores, Indonesia, has risen to at least 47, with rescue teams struggling to reach remote communities due to landslides and damaged infrastructure. Hundreds of personnel have been deployed for search and recovery, while aftershocks and a separate 6.4 quake elsewhere in Indonesia caused additional panic. Authorities warn the toll may increase as communications are restored in cut-off areas.
